title: Use protected branches and merge checks
summary: A protected branch restricts who can push or merge. Merge checks can require useful conditions, such as a successful pipeline, before combining code.
introduction: A protected branch restricts who can push or merge. Merge checks can require useful conditions, such as a successful pipeline, before combining code. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain use protected branches and merge checks
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A protected branch restricts who can push or merge. Merge checks can require useful conditions, such as a successful pipeline, before combining code.

blocks.title: Use protected branches and merge checks

blocks.text: The plan combines access rules and evidence checks. Available settings vary by GitLab version, plan and project configuration.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a successful pipeline does not replace reading the diff.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Access permission and review readiness are different questions; both matter.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
